redFirst.basis: regression task over an inline suite: the guard and its --selftest are one file, so the red-first helper cannot lay the test over HEAD without the fix (the case that turned this task from tdd to regression). The red was observed by hand before the fix: gr70/gr70b failed 99/100 on the unfixed guard-release.py.

outcome.descriptive: The release guard finds a publishing git or gh command however it is spelled - past assignments, wrappers, git's global options and a shell's -c - and its own suite runs under a temp path holding a space.
outcome.technical: Written by the orchestrator (guard command-reading code). .claude/hooks/guard-release.py: `_GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE`, `_GIT_REPO_MOVES` and `_git_verb` read git's verb past its global options; `_words_publishers` reads publishing commands from shell words, recursing through `sh -c` via `_config._handed_command` and finding the program past assignments and wrappers via `_config.program_candidates`/`program_name`; `_publishers` takes that word reading and falls back to the regex reading only when the command will not tokenise; `_tag_creates_words` grades tag creation from words. Cases gr70/gr70b pin the spellings that passed unread before (assignment and wrapper prefixes, `git -C <dir> tag`, `sh -c 'git push --tags'`). The suite's gr34/gr34c fixtures now quote the worktree path (`shlex.quote`), so a temp path holding a space builds the same command, and the file's SPACED_EXEMPT row in tools/sweep-selftests.py is removed - the spaced sweep leg runs it and it passes. Sweep and spaced sweep 331/331 files ok; gate-parity ok.
